Important information for proposers and award recipients

All proposals must be submitted in accordance with the requirements specified in the funding opportunity and in the Proposal & Award Policies & Procedures Guide (PAPPG) and its supplements.

All NSF grants and cooperative agreements are subject to the applicable set of NSF award terms and conditions.

NSF has updated its research security policies for NSF funded projects.

Supports research in differential geometry, geometric group theory, geometric methods in modern mathematical physics, geometric partial differential equations and related geometric topics.

Supports research in differential geometry, geometric group theory, geometric methods in modern mathematical physics, geometric partial differential equations and related geometric topics.

Synopsis

Research supported by the Geometric Analysis program includes the areas listed below. This is not a comprehensive list. Proposals on other relevant topics will also be considered. Contact the program if you have questions. 

·      differential geometry

·      geometric group theory

·      geometric partial differential equations and variational principles

·      geometric methods in modern mathematical physics

·      contact, symplectic and complex geometry

·      aspects of global analysis, including convex, integral and information geometries

·      geometric data analysis

 

Conferences 

Proposals for conferences, workshops, summer/winter schools and similar activities in Geometric Analysis must be submitted to the MPS Mathematical Sciences Research Programs solicitation using the "conference" or “travel” proposal type in research.gov. Proposers should select Geometric Analysis as the program of interest. For proposals seeking no more than $50,000, submit at least six months in advance of the conference or workshop date. For proposals seeking more than $50,000, submit at least nine months in advance of the conference or workshop date.
